rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Action 4 Create 5 Learn 6 Archive 7 Excavate 8 Search 9 Timeline 10 Decline 11 Game End Overview Have the most points after someone obtains 14 cards in their Past Turn On your turn, you will perform three steps • Action • Timeline • Decline Action You may take 2 the same or different actions between: • Create • Learn • Excavate • Archive • Search Create This allows you to play either a Monument or an Artifact card If you play a Monument, discard cards from your hand equal to its cost or it may be free. Place it in the numbered space indicated by the circle. Place a number of knowledge tokens on it equal to the Knowledge symbol. If it has an instant effect, apply as much as possible. A monument can be played in a space other than where it wishes as long as it does not contain the lock symbol, and you discard extra cards equal to the difference between where it wants to be and where you want to put it e.g. if it's a 4 and you want it in space 6, discard an extra 2 cards. For each numbered area, place your first monument on the lower space, and your second monument on the upper space, you cannot have a third monument for each numbered space. If you have two monuments in a numbered space, and the lower monument is removed due to some effect, slide the upper monument down so it becomes the new lower monument. Any effects which mention adjacency only affect orthogonal adjacency. If you play an Artifact, play it in one of your 5 starting artifact spaces on your player board. Once all 5 spaces are taken, you cannot play more artifacts until some effect gives you an empty space again. Learn This allows you to obtain Technologies Some technologies have requirements in a faded box, others have no requirements You are free to take any technology you meet the requirements for Some technologies will have instant effects You do not refill the technologies when you take one, only when a tile contains a single technology is it discarded and refilled Archive This lets you discard any number of cards you wish and discard 1 knowledge off a Monument for each discarded, you cannot discard more cards than you have knowledge on Monuments It's good to clear Knowledge off your Monuments, but also keeping it may be required for certain card conditions Excavate Rotate Monument cards in your Past, for each rotated draw 2 new cards Monuments do NOT auto-straighten, so to do this again you'll need either play more cards or effects which straighten Monuments Search This allows you to draw a single card, which makes it a lot weaker than the Excavate action where you may draw as many pairs of cards as monuments you wish to rotate, this action is intended as a last desperate resort Regardless of how you draw cards, you can never have more than 10 cards in hand, you may not draw and discard, but are instead blocked from drawing in either way if you hold 10 cards (or 9 and try to Excavate) Timeline After you've taken your two actions, Timeline phase begins Trigger the effects of any active cards you wish (a card in the Past is NOT active) Decline Check for Monuments in Zone 1, if there are any, they decline Some Monuments will have effects when they go into decline, others don't, once finished declining they are in the Past and won't have any effects Any knowledge on a declined Monument goes into your Lost Knowledge Zone If there were 2 Monuments in Zone 1, you pick one to fully decline before declining the other, they are then both placed in the Past If there are 7 Monuments in your Past, flip over one of the level I tech tiles to its Level II side If there are 14 Monuments in your Past, end game is triggered After which, slide all your monuments along one space, so 4's go into 3 and so on, 2's which now turned into 1's do not decline until your NEXT decline phase Game End The game end is triggered when a player moves their 14th monument into their Past. (It is possible to have 15 Monuments in your past, if on one turn you had 13, moved 2 from 2 to 1, then moved those 2 again from 1 to Past) Continue until an equal number of turns has been played. • Monuments in the Past score players based on the number in the middle band • Past Monuments may have effects which give a player bonus points • Level II Technologies will award additional points • Score 1VP for Monuments left in the Timeline • Lose 1VP for each Knowledge token in your Lost Knowledge Zone The player with the most points wins! (If tied, the player with the fewest Lost Knowledge wins.)

---

[Rating: 1/10] If you dont get the right cards, you nealry cant do anything. Its fully based on luck, worst game i ever played. If an opponent gets early the right artifacts becomes unbeatable.

[Rating: 2/10] The textbook definition of multi-player solitaire and the exact type of gameplay that I despise in a game. Won't ever play or recommend unless MPS is your thing.

[Rating: 2/10] After 2 play sessions, live and on BGA, I would rate it 4/10 – an intriguing mechanical premise with delayed card sequencing, but it lacks strategic depth and fails to evolve into a cohesive and substantively engaging game.  +2 more plays and you have seen it all. The game is really just about the "knowledge" management, thus completely uninteresting. (2/10) Copy sold!

[Rating: 3/10] Multiplayer solitaire except for a common tableau of cards and shitty take that effects. I just hate this kind of design. It's such a shame, because otherwise it has some neat stuff in it, although even the cards moving is underwhelming.

[Rating: 3/10] I had high hopes for this game but they were all swiftly dashed. While the key mechanism of placing out monuments and using the order and manner in which they decline initially seemed interesting, in reality it soon proved annoyingly fiddly and actually rather dull. There is also a frankly ludicrous disparity in utility between a great many of the cards which leaves the game prone to being massively impacted by sheer luck. Apparently Race for the Galaxy was a big inspiration for this but this is a far inferior product which lacks the snappiness, genuine scope for clever play and more engaging 

[Rating: 3/10] Overhype anyone? The maiden voyage was a disaster and I'm not sure I want to bother with another try. This is an AP trap made worse with wildly varying turn lengths based on what actions you are performing. I also didn't see anything that distinguishes it from the flood of games that have 1000 unique cards that force you to read the whole game rather than interacting with people. There is an activity called reading that is better than board games if I want to do that. Reading a book also takes less time than slogging through this.

[Rating: 3/10] My initial play of this was pretty good (base game), incorporating the expansion however, I ran into a problem that completely obliterated my desire to play it: the deck is too fucking big, and the comobo's are mostly an afterthought. The central idea of a depleting tableau is interesting, but the problem is that it's so focused on this aspect that all other considerations for gameplay are basically tossed aside. This would be totally fine, if you didn't have to mill the deck constantly to get a reasonable hand of cards, which seem to otherwise end up as disparate and completely non cohesive. 

[Rating: 3/10] Tableau builder where your cards get conveyored into history. The ancient architecture theme is a potentially rich one, but it's wasted and narratively opaque in practice, with the token/card-moving engines you build feeling almost completely abstract. They're not very interesting mechanically either.

[Rating: 3/10] Engine building game, but flawed engine. If you start with bad cards and the others get good cards you can never come back. I was picking my nose for 70 minutes while my friends enjoyed the streamlined engine.

[Rating: 3/10] Boring interactions, you have nothing to do in other players turn and it  makes long, boring waiting time between your turns. As an engine builder, it lacks choices and does not provide good feeling that you actually improving anything. You cant follow other players victory points, you have absolutely no idea who is leading. No theme. Overall it is not a good game. 3/10
